idiom_name: IHostedService/BackgroundService lifecycle hooks on the .NET Generic Host
implementation_notes: The .NET Generic Host owns startup and shutdown: it builds the service provider, starts hosted services sequentially and calls StartAsync/ExecuteAsync and StopAsync on your implementation, so you override hooks instead of writing the run loop. The classic framework base class survives here - BackgroundService is the abstract skeleton and ExecuteAsync is the hook the host invokes - which is the right form when the component needs a framework-managed lifetime and dependency injection. For request-shaped or small surfaces the delegate form with minimal APIs is lighter.
pitfalls: StartAsync and ExecuteAsync run on the host's schedule: blocking work in StartAsync delays every later service, and an ExecuteAsync that ignores the stopping token is killed at the shutdown timeout.
Exceptions escaping a hosted service's lifecycle methods surface through the host's shutdown path, not at the call site that started the work.

variants.name: Route-handler delegates (ASP.NET Core minimal APIs)
variants.idiom_name: MapGet/MapPost route handlers invoked by ASP.NET Core routing
variants.implementation_notes: Minimal APIs register delegates with Map{Verb}; the routing framework invokes the matching handler when a request arrives, and app.Run() hands control to the server loop, so no application code owns the request sequence. The framework base class (Controller/BackgroundService) is replaced by a function value plus registration, which is idiomatic for small HTTP surfaces and composes well with endpoint filters. Use the class-based hook form when the component needs DI-managed lifetime, several shared endpoints or rich metadata.
pitfalls: Route handlers resolve services from the container per request; capturing a scoped service in a singleton lambda causes lifetime bugs, so take dependencies as handler parameters.
Registration order and endpoint metadata decide what runs (auth, filters, route precedence), so a shadowed or missing route only fails at request time.
